onsite.goal: Agree a build plan to move checkout personalization to Workers
onsite.intake: Submitted by the account executive: goal, stakeholders (head of platform engineering, checkout team lead), the decision Northwind needs to make (build checkout personalization on Workers or keep the legacy service), and timing (before the holiday code freeze).
agenda: 09:00 – The decision for today and what success looks like
10:45 – Target design: personalization logic on Workers
13:00 – Working session: build one personalization rule together
15:00 – Build plan, risks, and owners on both sides
16:00 – Readout with the head of platform engineering
prep_checklist: Review usage data and On-track % trend
Get the current checkout architecture diagram
Build a working demo of one personalization rule
Confirm the decision makers attend the readout
Check last year's holiday usage before setting targets
onsite.execution: Working sessions, not a product tour: agree on a build plan and name owners on both sides before the day ends.
follow_ups: Send a written summary within 2 business days
Track actions in the engagement tracker
FDE builds with Northwind's developers in the Commit Burn Sprint
onsite.success_metric: First workload in production within 6 weeks; On-track % back above {on_track_warn} within the quarter

program.name: Commit Burn Sprint
program.trigger: Commit at risk alert and unused commit of {sprint_min_unused} or more
program.owner: SA leads; FDE joins for Deep engagement accounts
steps: Week 1: review usage, pick 1–2 workloads to move, agree success criteria
Weeks 2–5: build and test with the customer's developers; weekly check-ins
Week 6: first workload in production; review results with the customer
program.success_metric: On-track % back above {on_track_warn} within one quarter

handoff.owner: When all four tests pass, the program moves to the team that agreed to own it, and strategy moves on to the next new idea.
ready_when: It has a clear trigger and steps that others can follow
It has run with enough accounts to show a result
Its impact is measured against the comparison group
A team has agreed to own it, with time to run it
